# A module zip carries no generated file. So a dependency that generates part
# of its own API ships a package the compiler reads as empty, and the consumer
# fails on a symbol the dependency's source never declares. cmd/go runs that
# dependency's own directives first.

env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod

# The package declares what it produces, and the zip does not carry it.
go mod download example.com/generated
! exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# The build reads the generated copy rather than the empty package.
go build ./...

# The generated tree is in the module cache, beside the module it comes from,
# rather than inside it: go.sum pins the bytes the proxy served, and a generated
# file in that tree would report every module as modified.
exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/cache/generate/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go
! exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go
go mod verify

# GOGENERATEDEPS=off reads exactly what was fetched, so the symbol is undefined.
env GOGENERATEDEPS=off
! go build ./...
stderr 'undefined: lang\.Name'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.16

require example.com/generated v1.0.0
-- use.go --
package use

import "example.com/generated/lang"

var Name = lang.Name()
